findings.title: Reminders without a destination or message never consume a retry
findings.body: When `message` is empty or `sendTo` is falsy, this condition skips scheduling, but neither the failure branch nor the catch increments `retryCount`. The reminder therefore remains unscheduled and is selected again on every cron run, so reminders with a missing phone number (or message) are never removed by the retry limit.

findings.title: Concurrent failures can lose retry increments
findings.body: This writes an absolute count derived from the value read earlier. If two cron invocations process the same reminder concurrently, both can read the same `retryCount` and write the same incremented value; two failed scheduling attempts can thus leave the count at 1 rather than 2, delaying or preventing cleanup under repeated overlap. Use an atomic increment or otherwise ensure only one worker processes a reminder at a time.
